stem:
Sucrose is a white crystalline solid, $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$. In reaction **Z**, sucrose reacts with water in the presence of a catalyst, aqueous hydrochloric acid, to form glucose and fructose.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Suggest a name for the reaction that occurs when sucrose reacts with water to form glucose and fructose.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
If no catalyst is added in reaction **Z**, the reaction is very slow.

Label the Boltzmann distribution to show the effect of adding a catalyst to the sample of sucrose and water molecules at constant temperature.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Explain your labelled diagram.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Both fructose and glucose contain chiral centres.
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *chiral centre*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On the diagram of the fructose molecule, label all the chiral centres with an asterisk (*).

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the empirical formula of fructose.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *enthalpy change of combustion*.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write the equation for the complete combustion of sucrose.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The enthalpy change of reaction **Z**, $\Delta H_{\text{r}}$, can be calculated using the enthalpy change of combustion data given in the table.

| substance | enthalpy change of combustion, $\Delta H_{\text{c}} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| sucrose | $-5643$ |
| glucose | $-2805$ |
| fructose | $-2810$ |

Use the data in the table to calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction occurring when sucrose reacts with water, $\Delta H_{\text{r}}$. You should draw a labelled Hess' cycle to show your working.
